notes: Evals 1-3: review a fixture with exactly 3 planted structural violations (listed only here) plus decoys. Evals 4-5: generative — implement a feature in a trimmed copy of the real server/src (fixtures/server-base: a clean module pr-history, a legacy module agents, container, mocks, schema); graded on the resulting diff. Runs must see only their copy of the fixture, never this file.

evals.name: review-stale-pulls-module
evals.prompt: I've added a new `stale-pulls` module to the API server — the files are in server/src/modules/stale-pulls/. Please review it before I open a PR: what should I change and how?
evals.expected_output: A review that finds the three planted violations (DB query in a route handler, process.env read in the service, service constructing its own repository) with concrete fixes, and does not flag the type-only row import in helpers.ts.
planted: routes.ts: GET /repos/:id/stale-pulls/count imports drizzle-orm + db schema and queries app.container.db inside the handler (also re-implements the staleness cutoff)
service.ts: reads process.env.STALE_PULL_DAYS in the constructor
service.ts: takes Db and builds `new StalePullsRepository(db)` itself (imports the repository class); wiring.ts passes container.db
decoys: helpers.ts: `import type { PullRow }` in a pure row → type mapper used by the repository (allowed)
domain.ts / constants.ts: pure staleness helpers (correct placement)
assertions: Flags the /stale-pulls/count handler in routes.ts for querying the DB directly (drizzle-orm / schema / app.container.db in the route) and proposes moving the query into the repository behind the StalePullStore port plus a service method
Flags the process.env.STALE_PULL_DAYS read in service.ts and proposes passing the value in from config through wiring.ts (constructor option) instead of reading env in the service
Flags that StalePullsService constructs its own StalePullsRepository from a Db (importing the repository class) and proposes injecting the StalePullStore port from wiring.ts
Points out that the count handler duplicates the staleness rule (its own day arithmetic / default 14) instead of reusing the domain staleCutoff function and the constant
Does not report helpers.ts importing PullRow with `import type` as a violation

evals.name: review-slack-notifications-module
evals.prompt: Here's my implementation of posting a review summary to Slack when a run finishes: server/src/modules/notifications/. Does the structure hold up? Tell me what you'd fix and how the fixed version should look.
evals.expected_output: A review that finds the three planted violations (Slack SDK used directly in the service, whole Container passed to the service, another module's repository imported) with fixes that follow port → adapter → mock → container getter, and does not flag the job payload parsing in wiring.ts.
planted: service.ts: imports `WebClient` from @slack/web-api and calls chat.postMessage directly — external I/O with no port, adapter or mock
service.ts: constructor takes `container: Container` and reads container.config.slackChannel and container.secrets (service locator)
wiring.ts + service.ts: import ReviewRepository from ../reviews/repository.js (another module's data layer, also as a type in the core)
decoys: wiring.ts: job handler parses its payload with Zod and makes one service call (correct)
assertions: Flags the direct @slack/web-api WebClient usage in service.ts and proposes a port shaped by the use case (e.g. ReviewNotifier / ChatNotifier) implemented by an adapter under src/adapters/<port>/slack.ts
Mentions adding a mock/fake for the new notifier port and a container getter with an override slot, so tests do not hit Slack

Flags passing the whole Container into NotificationsService (service locator for config.slackChannel / secrets) and proposes narrow explicit dependencies (notifier, channel value) supplied by wiring.ts

Flags importing ReviewRepository from ../reviews/repository.js (in wiring and as a type in the service) as a cross-module dependency and proposes a facade from the reviews module's types.ts resolved through the container, or a port owned by the notifications module
Does not report the Zod-parsed job handler in wiring.ts (payload parsed at the edge, one service call) as a violation
acceptable_extra_findings: domain.ts returns a Slack Block Kit shaped SlackMessage (vendor-shaped type in the domain); flagging it is legitimate

evals.name: review-risk-badge-diff
evals.prompt: Review risk-badge.diff before I commit it (it adds a PR risk badge to the API server; the migration for the risk_badges table is in a separate commit). Anything wrong structurally?
evals.expected_output: A review that finds the three planted violations (risk thresholds computed in SQL in the repository, FastifyReply/HTTP status handling in the service, module-local repository registered in the DI container) with concrete fixes, and does not object to the registry line.
planted: repository.ts: the business rule (any CRITICAL → red, ≥3 WARNING → amber, else green) is a SQL CASE inside the repository
service.ts: imports FastifyReply, takes `reply` and sends a 404 itself instead of throwing an AppError subclass
platform/container.ts: registers the module-local RiskBadgeRepository as a container getter; wiring.ts reads container.riskBadgeRepository
decoys: modules/index.ts: one import + one entry to register the module (required footprint)
assertions: Flags the red/amber/green thresholds computed in the repository's SQL CASE as a business rule in infrastructure and proposes a pure domain function (with named threshold constants) while the repository returns only the counts
Flags RiskBadgeService importing FastifyReply and sending the 404 itself, and proposes throwing NotFoundError (AppError) so the shared error handler maps it and the route stays a one-call handler
Flags the platform/container.ts change that registers the module-local RiskBadgeRepository and proposes constructing it in the module's wiring.ts from container.db instead
Does not report the modules/index.ts registration (one import + one entry) as a violation
Does not ask to refactor the pre-existing AgentsRepository / ReviewRepository container entries as part of this change
acceptable_extra_findings: splitting computeAndSave's transaction once the level rule moves to the domain (it follows from the planted fix)

evals.name: implement-hot-files-endpoint
evals.prompt: Add an endpoint GET /repos/:id/hot-files to the API server: the 10 files touched by the most pull requests opened in the last 30 days, and for each file the number of CRITICAL findings reported on it across those PRs. Implement it in server/.
evals.expected_output: A new self-contained module (routes → wiring → service → port → repository) registered with one line in modules/index.ts; window and limit as named domain constants; no container, schema or legacy-pattern changes.
assertions: Puts the feature in a new module folder under server/src/modules/; outside that folder the only changed file is modules/index.ts (one import + one entry) — platform/container.ts, db/schema and other modules are untouched
The new routes.ts handler declares Zod params and response schemas, gets the workspace via getContext and makes exactly one service call; routes.ts imports nothing from drizzle-orm or db/

The SQL lives in the module's repository, which implements an interface declared in the module's ports.ts; ports.ts uses module/contract types only (no drizzle-orm, no db/schema values, no *Row types) and the query is scoped by workspaceId

The 30-day window and the top-10 limit are named constants (constants.ts or domain.ts), and the cutoff date is computed outside SQL (domain/service, with an injectable clock or `now` argument) and passed into the repository

The service is constructed in the module's wiring.ts with explicit dependencies (the port implementation, a clock); the service class does not take Container, does not import repository.ts or db/, and does not read process.env
The change does not copy the legacy pattern of the agents module (service constructed with `new XService(app.container)` or building its own repository)

evals.name: implement-deepl-translation
evals.prompt: Add on-demand translation of a review finding with the DeepL API: POST /findings/:id/translate with body { targetLang } returns the finding's title and rationale translated. The DeepL API key must be configurable the same way as our other API keys. Implement it in server/.
evals.expected_output: A Translator port shaped by the use case, a DeepL adapter under src/adapters/, a fake in mocks.ts, a lazy container getter with an override slot reading the key through SecretsProvider, and a new module whose service receives the translator and its store explicitly from wiring.ts.
assertions: Declares a translator port shaped by the use case (e.g. translate(texts, targetLang)) with no DeepL-specific types, in the new module's ports.ts or a server-wide ports location — and implements it in an adapter file under server/src/adapters/<name>/ (e.g. adapters/translator/deepl.ts), not inside the module folder
The adapter maps DeepL/HTTP failures to ExternalServiceError and a missing key to ConfigError (or equivalent AppError subclasses), so no raw fetch/HTTP error escapes the adapter
Adds a fake/mock translator to adapters/mocks.ts (or next to the other mocks) and a container getter for the translator with an override slot in ContainerOverrides
Reads the DeepL key through SecretsProvider (container.secrets.get(...)) in the container/adapter construction path; no process.env read for the key anywhere

The new service receives the translator (or a lazy resolver function) and its finding store as explicit constructor dependencies built in the module's wiring.ts; it does not take Container and does not import another module's repository or the concrete DeepL adapter
The route declares Zod params, body and response schemas and makes one service call; routes.ts has no drizzle-orm/db imports and no adapter imports
